chapters.title: AI in endpoint management and wrap-up

takeaways: Treat Microsoft licensing as an architecture decision, not a procurement task, and start with a licence audit and capability mapping.
Use Intune as the enforcement layer for configuration and security policies and Defender as the detection and response layer, built on an identity-first baseline.
Review licence usage, policy coverage and open gaps quarterly to avoid paying for unused add-ons or overlapping tools.
hook: Many organizations buy Microsoft 365 E3, E5 or E7 licences without knowing which capabilities they actually unlock. In this interview, Videsh Chavan, Head of EUC Engineering and Identity, explains for IT and security leaders how licensing, Intune, Defender and identity should work as one connected architecture. You get a practical five-step framework to close security gaps and control costs.
